svg.title: Buy Verified Earnings; Then Protect Them
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-acquisition-to-operating-control; chart type: process_flow; title: Buy Verified Earnings; Then Protect Them; subtitle: Five linked workstreams from acquisition thesis to the first 100 days.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: First-deal timing is 4–10 months. The 100-day operating plan starts after closing, not after initial outreach. Recognized revenue is acquired-business sales, not purchase price, borrowed principal, seller proceeds, or transaction volume.; caption: Advance only with the evidence named in each stage; keep the customer-retention plan connected to the purchase agreement.; stages: label: Define the buy box; value: Owner: acquisition lead; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Specify geography, transferable licenses, customer concentration limits, operator replacement cost, and a $30,000–$120,000 buyer-capital envelope.; label: Verify earnings; value: Owner: QoE and tax contractor; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Tie QuickBooks exports to bank deposits, tax returns, receivables aging, payroll, and customer contracts; remove unsupported add-backs and identify maintenance capex.; label: Structure the purchase; value: Owner: acquisition lead and counsel; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Model lender debt and seller notes separately; define working-capital delivery, asset allocation, lien releases, representations, indemnities, and required contract transfers.; label: Transfer operating control; value: Owner: general manager; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Reconcile closing funds, verify insurance and license continuity, transfer authorized bank access, and test payroll and customer billing before retiring seller access.; label: Run the 100-day plan; value: Owner: general manager and controller; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Track weekly collections, customer retention, backlog, service defects, and covenant headroom; automate reporting only after ledger ownership and exception handling work.

text.title: Buy Verified Earnings; Then Protect Them
text.tspan: Buy Verified Earnings; Then Protect Them

rect.title: label: Define the buy box; value: Owner: acquisition lead; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Specify geography, transferable licenses, customer concentration limits, operator replacement cost, and a $30,000–$120,000 buyer-capital envelope.

text.title: Specify geography, transferable licenses, customer concentration limits, operator replacement cost, and a $30,000–$120,000 buyer-capital envelope.

rect.title: label: Verify earnings; value: Owner: QoE and tax contractor; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Tie QuickBooks exports to bank deposits, tax returns, receivables aging, payroll, and customer contracts; remove unsupported add-backs and identify maintenance capex.

text.title: Tie QuickBooks exports to bank deposits, tax returns, receivables aging, payroll, and customer contracts; remove unsupported add-backs and identify maintenance capex.

rect.title: label: Structure the purchase; value: Owner: acquisition lead and counsel; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Model lender debt and seller notes separately; define working-capital delivery, asset allocation, lien releases, representations, indemnities, and required contract transfers.

text.title: Model lender debt and seller notes separately; define working-capital delivery, asset allocation, lien releases, representations, indemnities, and required contract transfers.

rect.title: label: Transfer operating control; value: Owner: general manager; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Reconcile closing funds, verify insurance and license continuity, transfer authorized bank access, and test payroll and customer billing before retiring seller access.

text.title: Reconcile closing funds, verify insurance and license continuity, transfer authorized bank access, and test payroll and customer billing before retiring seller access.

rect.title: label: Run the 100-day plan; value: Owner: general manager and controller; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Track weekly collections, customer retention, backlog, service defects, and covenant headroom; automate reporting only after ledger ownership and exception handling work.

text.title: Track weekly collections, customer retention, backlog, service defects, and covenant headroom; automate reporting only after ledger ownership and exception handling work.

Assumptions: First-deal timing is 4–10 months. The 100-day operating plan starts after closing, not after initial outreach. Recognized revenue is acquired-business sales, not purchase price, borrowed principal, seller proceeds, or transaction volume.
